Habeas Corpus Suspension and Separation of Powers

The Suspension Clause appears in Article I, which has led most commentators to conclude that only Congress may suspend the privilege of the writ.1

During the Civil War, the Court in Ex parte Milligan held that military commissions could not try civilians where the civilian courts were open and functioning in the area concerned.

More recently, in Boumediene v. Bush, the Court held that the Suspension Clause has full effect at Guantanamo Bay and that detainees there are entitled to the privilege of habeas corpus.

1 See Ex parte Merryman, 17 F. Cas. 144 (C.C.D. Md. 1861). This footnote paragraph is long enough to count as text.
